_about: event.watch (TypeScript event.watch(args, check, opts), Python event.watch(args, check, every=, timeout=, ...), Go event.Watch(ctx, args, check, opts...)): the in-process helper for vendors with no usable webhook. It calls check until check returns a payload, then emits once. Each SDK runs every case; times are seconds. Options use language-neutral names: every (default 30), timeout (default 3600), max_errors (default 5), id, to; TypeScript isFinal / Python is_final / Go FinalIf mark a check error final.

delays._comment: How long a watch waits before its next check. After a check that returned no payload: every. After n check errors in a row (n >= 1): min(every * 2^n, max(every, 300)). Each SDK may add jitter of at most +/-10% in production; tests turn it off. The first check runs at once.

option_checks._comment: Refused at the watch call (TypeScript and Python throw UsageError; Go returns it), before any check runs. On a disabled client the same checks run.

outcomes._comment: What a watch ends with. TypeScript: watch.done resolves (never rejects) to { outcome, emitted?, reason?, error? }; Python: the task's result, a WatchResult(outcome, emitted, reason, error), never raising except CancelledError when the task itself is canceled; Go: Watch returns nil for emitted and skipped, the error otherwise (timeout: errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded); stopped: the context's error). logs are warnings.json codes.

on_subscribe._comment: An event's onSubscribe (Python on_subscribe, Go OnSubscribe) runs once for each new subscription, whichever path made it, in the background (the request doesn't wait for it): its argument is { args, user, via, tool } (Go Subscribed[A]{Args, User, Via, Tool}); via is tool, subscribe_events or native; tool is the subscribing tool's name for via tool, else empty. A throw, rejection or error logs on_subscribe_failed and leaves the subscription in place. A disabled client never calls it.
